children: African digital financial-services platform Airtel Money plans to float existing shares on the London Stock Exchange, in a boost to the U.K.'s ailing stock market.
Airtel Money expects an offering of at least $800 million of existing shares and is targeting a valuation of $8 billion to $9 billion, a person familiar with the transaction said.

The company, also known as Airtel Mobile Commerce, said Wednesday that the shares would be sold by existing shareholders and that upon admission it expects to have a free float of at least 10%. The company doesn't plan to raise new capital.
The London exchange has been hit by a drought of listings and a deluge of takeover deals and delistings, leading to an exodus of household names.

Last month, Apollo Global Management agreed to buy British budget airline easyJet after a protracted bidding war.  Meanwhile, Flutter Entertainment--which houses FanDuel, PokerStars, and Paddy Power among its brands--canceled its listing in London and made New York its main listing in August. In May, money-transfer company Wise moved its primary listing to New York, keeping a secondary listing in London. Rental company Ashtead canceled its primary London listing in March and switched to the New York Stock Exchange and rebranded as Sunbelt Rentals, the name of its U.S. business.

The U.K. government has implemented a series of reforms to make London a more competitive place to list. These have included lowering the percentage of shares that must be listed so entrepreneurs can retain a larger stake, and simplifying listing requirements and procedures.
Airtel Money reported earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $676 million in the fiscal year ended March, and currently has 53 million monthly active users.

As part of the sale, International Finance Corp. agreed to buy a stake of up to 67.2 million pounds, equivalent to $89.7 million, from shareholders. Shares will also be offered to U.K. residents, with the full details of the offer price expected in mid-October, it said.
Airtel Africa, which owns 77.85% of Airtel Money's shares, said in a separate release that it expects to remain a long-term shareholder.
Airtel Money operates in 13 markets in sub-Saharan Africa, where traditional banking infrastructure is underdeveloped.
